critical_code_review_comments: Correct architectural choice in scoreField: `useFull = rule.length>=2` scopes section-party token (from <legend>) ONLY to multi-token rules. Single-token party rules like ['first party']/['second party'] stay LOCAL-only, which is exactly what prevents the duty-section fields (which sit after the Second Party fieldset) from being misclassified as Second Party name. This is defense-in-depth paired with the neg-token guard.
sectionParty() uses compareDocumentPosition with (pos&2)&&!(pos&8) — correctly selects only strictly PRECEDING headings and excludes ancestor containers of the input. Good.

setVal SELECT still uses bidirectional substring match (both ways); not a current issue because mock Paid-by options are disjoint, but if the real SHCIL page has overlapping option labels (e.g., 'First Party' vs 'First Party (Buyer)'), the first match wins. Low-risk latent issue.

FIELDS mapping is being transported through a template-literal regex; consider exporting FIELDS separately so a jest/vitest unit test can import it directly and run scoreField against synthetic DOMs without regex extraction.

rca of the issue: Prior bug: when the real SHCIL form uses <fieldset><legend>First Party Details</legend> + generic 'Address Line 1' labels, each input's local context never contained the 'first party' token, so the ['first party','address line 1'] rule failed and Address Line 1 stayed blank. FIX in /app/frontend/src/lib/bookmarklet.js: (1) sectionParty(el) walks document headings (legend/caption/th/h1-6/strong/b/[class*=head|section|title|group]) and uses compareDocumentPosition((pos&2)&&!(pos&8)) to find the nearest strictly-preceding non-ancestor party heading, returning 'first party' or 'second party'. (2) scoreField uses full context (local+section) ONLY for rules with length>=2, so multi-token party rules can satisfy the party token from the section heading, while single-token party rules (loose name fallback) still require the party token in LOCAL context — preventing leakage into the duty-section fields which sit after the Second Party fieldset. (3) neg-token guard remains, so even if a party token were present via section, address/mobile/email tokens in local context still block *_name from matching those fields. Verified on mock: section-aware address fills correctly, duty fields untouched by Second Party name, empties stay blank.
